subject: Final network cutover verification & smoke test report — Acme Corp VPC Private Deployment
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, dylan_brooks@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Cc: 
Date: 2026-05-28T09:12:00Z
Subject: Final network cutover verification & smoke plan for Acme private deployment

Team —

We have an agreed cutover window for Acme's private VPC deployment this week (target: 2026-06-01 02:00-04:00 UTC). Before we proceed I want a short consolidated readiness check and a minimal smoke plan we can run immediately after cutover. Please treat this as the canonical list we will share with Acme and with Platform Ops. Key constraints: SLA requirement of 100ms median p95 for 512-token inference within the VPC, and encryption+customer KMS required for model keys.

Deliverables by EOD 2026-05-29:
- Network verification: inbound/outbound firewall rules, route tables, NAT/GW config, cross-VPC peering verification for logging.
- Certs & TLS: confirm cert issuance and reload steps on inference pods; include expiry windows.
- KMS/HSM: confirmation of key policies and rotation window (Marcus).
- Observability hooks: forward logs to Acme SIEM, ensure traces have tenant tag.
- Minimal smoke tests: health check, sample 1k-token generation (latency and correctness), KV cache warm start, prefix caching validation.
- Rollback plan: immediate fallback to hosted Redwood API routing policy (how to flip, who executes).

I'm assigning tasks inline:
- Laura: network diagram + verification checklist and sample iptables/SGs
- Marcus: KMS/HSM policy + key-access runbook
- Dylan: smoke test harness, expected pass/fail criteria, and CSV template for results
- Lauren: customer communication + post-cutover escalation path (who to call, PagerDuty runbook)

Keep responses concise. We'll assemble a single PDF to send to Acme by 2026-05-30 18:00 UTC.

Thanks —
Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Platform Engineering
Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, dylan_brooks@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: 2026-05-29T16:43:00Z
Subject: Re: Final network cutover verification & smoke plan for Acme private deployment

Vivek / team —

Attached the updated network diagram (network-diagram-acme-v2.pdf) and a short checklist. Summary:
- Border firewall: ACME's edge team confirmed the 10.240.0.0/16 prefix will be allowed outbound to Redwood egress IPs: 34.210.110.45, 34.210.110.46.
- Inbound control plane: We only allow port 443 from Acme management IP set (ACME-MGMT-POOL) to the control-plane NLB; inference traffic uses private peering.
- Route tables: Transit gateway is configured; tested via traceroute from Acme bastion -> inference service; latency within expected range (~4–12ms).
- NAT: Confirmed ephemeral NAT for model download step; will be disabled post-pull via automation step in runbook-cutover-v2.md.

Open items:
- We need to confirm SNAT behavior for health-check probes (Dylan to validate with smoke harness).
- We'll include a fail-closed firewall rule that will be removed only if tests pass.

Attaching network-diagram-acme-v2.pdf (see attachments).

-Laura
Laura Bennett
Principal Network Engineer, Redwood

From: Anita Rao <anita.rao@acme-corp.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: cloudops@edge-partners.com
Date: 2026-05-30T11:20:15Z
Subject: Re: Final network cutover verification & smoke plan for Acme private deployment

Thanks for the checklist and diagram — this looks good. A couple of last-minute asks from our infra/security team:

1) Can you confirm the exact outbound ports used by the inference runtime during peak loads (we need to open them for our egress firewall)?
2) For TLS certs: does Redwood perform OCSP stapling on the control-plane certs or should we expect the client to validate via CA endpoints?
3) During model pull (initialization window), will there be any short-lived outbound connections to model bucket endpoints in us-east-1? If so, can you provide FQDNs/IP ranges so our proxy allowlist can be updated?

We are on standby for the cutover window. Also looping in our partner contact (cloudops@edge-partners.com) who will assist with transit gateway checks.

Best,
Anita Rao
Head of Infrastructure, Acme Corp
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, laura_bennett@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: 2026-06-01T02:05:42Z
Subject: Cutover execution & smoke-results-20260601.csv (prelim)

Team — cutover executed 2026-06-01 02:00 UTC. Below are the smoke test highlights (full CSV attached):

Smoke summary (short):
- Health check endpoint (/v1/health) returned 200 within 300ms for 100 probes. PASS
- 512-token generation @ sample prompt: median latency 86ms, p95 142ms. PASS (within SLA)
- KV cache warm start: observed 95% cache hit after two warm-up requests. PASS
- Prefix caching: validated for two tenants including Acme; sample outputs matched golden set (accuracy check). PASS
- Model pull step: initial pull created short-lived connections to s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com and models.redwood-internal.net (expected). We used AWS egress IP 18.205.xx.18 for the transfer.

Outstanding (minor) issues:
- Observability tags: one trace from a canary pod was missing tenant_id tag — root cause: env var not set in that pod; fix pushed and verifier ran successfully.
- SNAT: health probes from Acme bastion returned different source IP due to NAT gateway; Laura to add note in runbook.

Attachments: smoke-results-20260601.csv (contains per-probe latency and success flags).

Next steps:
- I'll push the final CSV into the Drive link and mark the runbook as complete.
- Lauren, please send the customer-facing brief and the escalation contacts.

Dylan Brooks
Platform Reliability Engineer, Redwood
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: anita.rao@acme-corp.com, cloudops@edge-partners.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, dylan_brooks@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: 2026-06-01T09:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Final network cutover verification & smoke plan for Acme private deployment — Go-live confirmed

Anita / Acme team —

Thank you. Cutover has been completed and smoke tests passed. Summary for your ops team:
- Cutover time: 2026-06-01 02:00 UTC (completed within 5 min of window).
- Health checks: 100/100 probes green.
- Latency: median 86ms (512 tokens), p95 142ms.
- Model pull: required short-lived egress to s3.us-east-1 and models.redwood-internal.net (we will provide IP ranges for final allowlist).
- KMS: key policies validated; rotation not triggered.
- Observability: logs forwarded to Acme SIEM and traces have tenant tag (minor pod fix verified).

Runbook and artifacts: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/Acme-PrivateDeployment/Runbooks/runbook-cutover-v2.md
JIRA: JIRA-OPS-4521
Attachments: network-diagram-acme-v2.pdf, smoke-results-20260601.csv

If anything pops up over the next 48 hours we will treat it as Sev2 and escalate to the platform on-call per the runbook.

Thanks to the whole team for the fast execution. Laura, Marcus, Dylan, Lauren — special callout for rapid turnaround.

-Vivek
